arxiv-1810-07935.title: Zhongdi Cen, Jian Huang
arxiv-1810-07935.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by ∗. An efficient numerical method for a time-fractional diffusion equation Abstract: A reaction-diffusion problem with a Caputo time derivative is considered. An integral discretization scheme on a graded mesh along with a decomposition of the exact solution is proposed. The truncation error estimate of the discretization scheme is derived by using the remainder formula of the linear interpolation and some inequality estimate techniques.

arxiv-2001-04061.title: Deep Learning based Pedestrian Inertial Navigation: Methods, Dataset and On-Device Inference
arxiv-2001-04061.creator: Changhao Chen, Peijun Zhao, Chris Xiaoxuan Lu, Wei Wang, Andrew Markham, Niki Trigoni
arxiv-2001-04061.description: Abstract Modern inertial measurements units (IMUs) are small, cheap, energy efficient, and widely employed in smart devices and mobile robots. Exploiting inertial data for accurate and reliable pedestrian navigation supports is a key component for emerging Internet-of-Things applications and services. Recently, there has been a growing interest in applying deep neural networks (DNNs) to motion sensing and location estimation.

arxiv-2205-10350.title: Lossless Acceleration for Seq2seq Generation with Aggressive Decoding
arxiv-2205-10350.creator: Tao Ge, Heming Xia, Xin Sun, Si-Qing Chen, Furu WeiMicrosoft {tage, sqchen, fuwei}@microsoft.com, {xiaheming, sunx5}@pku.edu.cn
arxiv-2205-10350.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Tao Ge, Heming Xia, Xin Sun, Si-Qing Chen, Furu WeiMicrosoft {tage, sqchen, fuwei}@microsoft.com, {xiaheming, sunx5}@pku.edu.cn. We study lossless acceleration for seq2seq generation with a novel decoding algorithm – Aggressive Decoding. Unlike the previous efforts (e.g., non-autoregressive decoding) speeding up seq2seq generation at the cost of quality loss, our approach aims to yield the identical (or better) generation compared with autoregressive decoding but in a significant speedup, achieved by innovative cooperation of aggressive decoding and verification that are both highly efficient due to parallel computing.

arxiv-2210-09291.title: Embodying the Glitch: Perspectives on Generative AI in Dance Practice Conference: The The CHI 2022 Workshop on Generative AI and HCI; ;
arxiv-2210-09291.creator: Benedikte Wallace, Charles Patrick Martin
arxiv-2210-09291.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Benedikte Wallace, Charles Patrick Martin. What role does the break from realism play in the potential for generative artificial intelligence as a creative tool? Through exploration of glitch , we examine the prospective value of these artefacts in creative practice. This paper describes findings from an exploration of AI-generated "mistakes" when using movement produced by a generative deep learning model as an inspiration source in dance composition. 0 0 footnotetext: Licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC BY 4.0).

arxiv-2308-09114.title: Thermodynamics of the three-dimensional black hole with torsion
arxiv-2308-09114.creator: Luis Avilés, Diego Hidalgo, Omar Valdivia
arxiv-2308-09114.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Luis Avilés, Diego Hidalgo, Omar Valdivia. The stationary black hole solution of a Chern-Simons model based on the semi-simple extension of the Poincaré gauge group is studied. The solution resembles the metric properties of the BTZ geometry but contains, in addition, non-vanishing torsion. The global structure of spacetime is characterized by three conserved charges: two associated with the mass and angular momentum and one extra constant triggered by spacetime torsion.

arxiv-2408-05690.title: Strong denoising of financial time-series
arxiv-2408-05690.creator: Matthias J. Feiler
arxiv-2408-05690.description: Abstract In this paper we introduce a method for significantly improving the signal to noise ratio in financial data. The approach relies on combining a target variable with different context variables and use auto-encoders (AEs) to learn reconstructions of the combined inputs.

arxiv-2410-00210.title: End-to-End Piano Performance-MIDI to Score Conversion with Transformers
arxiv-2410-00210.description: Abstract The automated creation of accurate musical notation from an expressive human performance is a fundamental task in computational musicology. To this end, we present an end-to-end deep learning approach that constructs detailed musical scores directly from real-world piano performance-MIDI files. We introduce a modern transformer-based architecture with a novel tokenized representation for symbolic music data.

arxiv-2410-13265.title: CONCENTRATED SUPERELLIPTICAL MARKET MAKER
arxiv-2410-13265.description: Abstract Initial Version: October 16, 2024 Current Version: November 25, 2024 Vasily Tolstikov E–mail: 0xeb567e5ac2feb7bbfc777e0bd18a8a34eb922e86@ethereum.mailchain.com SUMMARY: An automated market maker where the price can cross the zero bound into the negative price domain with applications in electricity, energy, and derivatives markets is presented.

arxiv-2502-07479.title: WebChecker: A Versatile EVL Plugin for Validating HTML Pages with Bootstrap Frameworks
arxiv-2502-07479.creator: Milind Cherukuri
arxiv-2502-07479.description: Abstract WebChecker is a plugin for Epsilon Validation Language (EVL), designed to validate both static and dynamic HTML pages utilizing frameworks like Bootstrap. By employing configurable EVL constraints, WebChecker enforces implicit rules governing HTML and CSS frameworks. The effectiveness of the plugin is demonstrated through its application on Bootstrap, the widely adopted HTML, CSS, and JavaScript framework.

arxiv-2503-02738.title: Variable-Friction In-Hand Manipulation for Arbitrary Objects via Diffusion-Based Imitation Learning
arxiv-2503-02738.creator: Qiyang Yan, Zihan Ding, Xin Zhou, Adam J. Spiers
arxiv-2503-02738.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Qiyang Yan, Zihan Ding, Xin Zhou, Adam J. Spiers. Dexterous in-hand manipulation (IHM) for arbitrary objects is challenging due to the rich and subtle contact process. Variable-friction manipulation is an alternative approach to dexterity, previously demonstrating robust and versatile 2D IHM capabilities with only two single-joint fingers. However, the hard-coded manipulation methods for variable friction hands are restricted to regular polygon objects and limited target poses, as well as requiring the policy to be tailored for each object.

arxiv-2506-01068.title: Free field construction of Heterotic string compactified on Calabi-Yau manifolds of Berglund-Hubsch type in the Batyrev-Borisov combinatorial approach
arxiv-2506-01068.creator: Alexander Belavin
arxiv-2506-01068.description: Abstract Heterotic string models in 4 4 -dimensions are the hybrid theories of a left-moving N = 1 N=1 fermionic string whose additional 6 6 -dimensions are compactified on a N = 2 N=2 SCFT theory with the central charge 9 9 , and a right-moving bosonic string, whose additional dimensions are also compactified on N = 2 N=2 SCFT

arxiv-2509-12531.title: Pre-trained Visual Representations Generalize Where it Matters in Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2509-12531.creator: Scott Jones, Liyou Zhou, Sebastian W. Pattinson
arxiv-2509-12531.description: Abstract In visuomotor policy learning, the control policy for the robotic agent is derived directly from visual inputs. The typical approach, where a policy and vision encoder are trained jointly from scratch, generalizes poorly to novel visual scene changes. Using pre-trained vision models (PVMs) to inform a policy network improves robustness in model-free reinforcement learning (MFRL).

arxiv-2511-17669.title: Empa: An AI-Powered Virtual Mentor for Developing Global Collaboration Skills in HPC Education
arxiv-2511-17669.creator: Ashish, Aparajita Jaiswal, Sudip Vhaduri, Niveditha Nerella, Shubham Jha
arxiv-2511-17669.description: Abstract . High-performance computing (HPC) and parallel computing increasingly rely on global collaboration among diverse teams, yet traditional computing curricula inadequately prepare students for cross-cultural teamwork essential in modern computational research environments. This paper presents Empa, an AI-powered virtual mentor that integrates intercultural collaboration training into undergraduate computing education.

arxiv-2602-14731.title: Systematic Review of Lightweight Cryptographic Algorithms CCS: Security and privacy Block and stream ciphers CCS: Security and privacy Public key encryption CCS: Security and privacy Digital signatures CCS: Security and privacy Key management CCS: Security and privacy Cryptanalysis and other attacks
arxiv-2602-14731.creator: Mohsin Khan, Elisavet Kozyri, Håvard Dagenborg
arxiv-2602-14731.description: Abstract . The emergence of small computing devices and the integration of processing units into everyday objects has made lightweight cryptography an essential part of the security landscape. Conventional cryptographic algorithms such as AES, RSA, and DES are unsuitable for resource-constrained devices due to limited processing power, memory, and battery.

pmc-10512837.title: Segmental and transmural motion of the rat myocardium estimated using quantitative ultrasound with new strategies for infarct detection
pmc-10512837.creator: Yinong Wang, Wufan Chen, Qing Wang
pmc-10512837.description: Introduction: The estimation of myocardial motion abnormalities has great potential for the early diagnosis of myocardial infarction (MI). This study aims to quantitatively analyze the segmental and transmural myocardial motion in MI rats by incorporating two novel strategies of algorithm parameter optimization and transmural motion index (TMI) calculation.

pmc-11382422.title: Dimension reduction, cell clustering, and cell–cell communication inference for single-cell transcriptomics with DcjComm
pmc-11382422.creator: Qian Ding, Wenyi Yang, Guangfu Xue, Hongxin Liu, Yideng Cai, Jinhao Que, Xiyun Jin, Meng Luo, Fenglan Pang, Yuexin Yang, Yi Lin, Yusong Liu, Haoxiu Sun, Renjie Tan, Pingping Wang, Zhaochun Xu, Qinghua Jiang
pmc-11382422.description: Advances in single-cell transcriptomics provide an unprecedented opportunity to explore complex biological processes. However, computational methods for analyzing single-cell transcriptomics still have room for improvement especially in dimension reduction, cell clustering, and cell–cell communication inference. Herein, we propose a versatile method, named DcjComm, for comprehensive analysis of single-cell transcriptomics.

pmc-11458929.title: Autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis presenting as localized multifocal GGOs: A case report
pmc-11458929.creator: Koichi Honda, Hirofumi Koike, Shin Tsutsui, Ryo Toya, Keitaro Matsumoto, Shinji Okano, Hirokazu Taniguchi, Kazuto Ashizawa
pmc-11458929.description: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP) is a rare disease, which is characterized by the alveolar accumulation of surfactant. A crazy-paving appearance on chest thin-section computed tomography (TSCT) is a characteristic feature of this disease. We report an unusual case of PAP, which presented as multiple localized ground glass opacites (GGOs) on TSCT in an 80-year-old female.

pmc-11476363.title: p66Shc Protein—Oxidative Stress Sensor or Redox Enzyme: Its Potential Role in Mitochondrial Metabolism of Human Breast Cancer
pmc-11476363.creator: Monika Prill, Vilma A. Sardão, Mateusz Sobczak, Dominika Nowis, Jedrzej Szymanski, Mariusz R. Wieckowski
pmc-11476363.description: Simple SummaryMitochondria as peculiar cellular “powerhouses” comprise a source of ATP produced by an oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) system. Additionally, they are implicated in several crucial cellular processes such as regulating the cellular levels of metabolites, Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) homeostasis, apoptosis, and many others.

pmc-11495203.title: Characteristics and Influencing Factors of Intra-Dialysis Blood Pressure Variability in Hemodialysis Patients: A Retrospective Study
pmc-11495203.creator: Haifan Xu, Xiaoshuang Wang, Miao Feng, Liqun Chen
pmc-11495203.description: ObjectiveTo investigate the correlation between background factors and blood pressure variability (BPV), and the prognostic value of intra-dialytic BPV metrics for cardiovascular death and all-cause mortality in hemodialysis (HD) patients.MethodsA retrospective study of 264 hD patients was followed up for 36 months.

pmc-11686609.title: Radiological and Clinical Outcomes of the Dovetailed Notch Scarf Osteotomy for Correcting the First Metatarsal Pronation in Moderate to Severe Hallux Valgus Deformity: A Comparative Study
pmc-11686609.creator: Ming-Zhu Zhang, Chao Wang
pmc-11686609.description: Category:Bunion; Midfoot/ForefootIntroduction/Purpose:The traditional scarf osteotomy (TSO) has limited ability to correct the first metatarsal pronation. A novel modification which we refer to as a “dovetailed notch Scarf osteotomy” (DNSO) has been developed to enhance the ability to correct coronal plane pronation.

pmc-12500519.title: Successful Transcatheter Edge‐To‐Edge Repair for Chronic Mitral Regurgitation Following Papillary Muscle Rupture
pmc-12500519.creator: Suguru Hirose, Manami Watahiki, Ikuko Shibasaki, Shigeru Toyoda
pmc-12500519.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Papillary muscle rupture (PMR) is a rare myocardial infarction complication, often associated with high surgical risk. This report highlights transcatheter edge‐to‐edge mitral valve repair as a feasible and less invasive alternative for high‐risk patients with chronic PMR.Keywords: mitral regurgitation, myocardial infarction, papillary muscle rupture, transcatheter edge‐to‐edge mitral valve repair Case Description Papillary muscle rupture (PMR) is a rare but severe complication of acute myocardial infarction (AMI), occurring in approximately 0.03% of cases [1].

pmc-12847474.title: Causal associations among albumin, C-reactive protein, body mass index, and the risk of colorectal cancer
pmc-12847474.creator: Xuecheng Xie, Zhigang Chen, Jian Song, Chaogang Huang, Chenglin Su, Hailong Liu, Qinyu Tian, Meng Xu, Haizhou Liu
pmc-12847474.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). PurposeA Mendelian randomization model analysis was employed to investigate the causal direction between CRP (C-reactive protein), Alb(albumin), and BMI(body mass index), as well as their impact on colorectal cancer (CRC) risk and postoperative prognosis.MethodsTwo-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) was conducted, with BMI set as the exposure variable and CRP, Alb, and CRC as the outcome variables, to determine if CRP and Alb mediate the causal relationship between BMI and CRC.

pmc-13474969.title: mFLIP: metabolic flux interval prediction
pmc-13474969.creator: Baris Can, Sadi Celik, Ali Cakmak
pmc-13474969.description: BackgroundUnderstanding cellular metabolism often involves an accurate estimation of metabolic fluxes–the rates at which metabolites are converted in biochemical pathways. Flux Variability Analysis (FVA) is the gold standard for computing reaction flux intervals. However, its reliance on linear programming makes it computationally intensive, often requiring hours or days for large cohorts on complex genome-scale metabolic network models.
